# Woge application coding guidance

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-spring-boot-agent-guidance.sh from template v1 and the Woge framework index. Do not edit generated copies. -->

This file describes the supported application shape for this exact scaffold. Humans and coding agents
use the same public APIs, compiler feedback, examples and documentation.

## Version-matched baseline

- Scaffold: `spring-boot` 0.3.1
- Woge: 0.1.0-SNAPSHOT
- Kotlin: 2.4.10
- Spring Boot: 4.1.1
- Build JDK: 21; produced JVM bytecode: Java 17
- Selected host: `webflux` (Spring Boot WebFlux)
- Frontend tooling: none is required. Playwright 1.62.1 is test-only; Tailwind and Vite
  are not installed.

Run `./gradlew wogeDev` while developing: it rebuilds on save, restarts Spring and refreshes the
browser. Run `./gradlew check` after application changes. `./gradlew wogeTasks --format=json` lists
the supported tasks and options as JSON. Change
`wogeSpringAdapter` in `gradle.properties` to `mvc` or `webflux` deliberately; do not mix both host
adapters in application code. Regenerate this file after changing the persisted host or a pinned
framework version; the normal test task rejects stale guidance.

`./gradlew wogeManifest` writes `.woge/manifest.json` from compiler metadata. Use the typed
`ApplicationManifest` model or generated `wogeDescriptors` lists; do not scan source or running
application objects. The manifest is generated, non-secret build output, not an endpoint registry.

Coding agents can start `./gradlew wogeDev --mcp` (experimental) and connect to the local MCP endpoint
described in `build/woge-dev/mcp.json`. Read the build cursor with `status`, edit, then call
`await_build` instead of polling the terminal or the page. See `docs/guides/development-mcp.md` in the
Woge repository.

## Keep the web platform visible

- Render semantic HTML on the server. Keep links, forms, methods, status codes and URLs recognizable.
- Write ordinary browser CSS in `src/main/resources/static`. String class names are intentional and
  remain compatible with plain CSS, CSS Modules and an optional later Tailwind pipeline.
- Deliver a useful native-navigation path before adding progressive enhancement. JavaScript may make a
  path faster; it must not become the only way to complete the core task.
- Prefer plain MPA navigation, optionally with native View Transitions/Speculation Rules. The separate
  enhanced-navigation helper is opt-in, not a router; managed action/live/deferred pages stay native.
- Keep domain and markup functions host-neutral. Spring request, response, Reactor and Servlet types
  belong only in the selected host adapter source set.

## Supported and unsupported shapes

| Concern | Use | Avoid |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Typed page input | `PageUseCase<ProjectInput>` with `PageRequest<ProjectInput>` | maps of strings or a Spring request inside the page |
| Markup | Woge element functions and `text(dynamicValue)` | HTML string concatenation or unaudited `raw(...)` |
| Page URL | `@WogeRoute("/projects/{project}")` on the input, then `ProjectPageRoute.url(input)` | string templates such as `"/projects/$slug?view=x"` |
| Other application URL | `applicationUrl("/assets/app.css")` passed to `url(...)` | unchecked dynamic URL strings in attributes |
| Native form | `form` with normal `method`, `action`, named controls and server validation | JavaScript-only submission or duplicated native/enhanced policy |
| Region target | `request.context.render.target(SummaryRegion)` and `regionPlaceholder(...)` | manual CSS selectors such as `#summary` as patch identity |
| Host boundary | a small route adapter calling the portable page port | Spring, Reactor or Servlet imports in reusable components |
| CSS | external modern CSS, class strings and bounded `declarations(...)` for inline values | a Kotlin catalog that hides normal CSS or unsanitized style data |

Typed page routes (`@WogeRoute`) and regions (`@WogeRegion`) are generated by the Woge KSP
processor. Register a route with `handlers.page(page, ProjectPageRoute)` at `ProjectPageRoute.path`.
`@WogeAction("stable-id")` generates typed action descriptors and explicit package registries.
Use `suspend fun save(command: Command): PageResult`; add `context: RequestContext` only when used.
Action IDs and route patterns are module-wide; collision diagnostics name both declarations.
For business-rule errors, build `FormValues.of(mapOf(field.name to listOf(command.text)))` from
selected display-safe text and pass it to `FormErrors`. Never preserve passwords or CSRF tokens.
Bind POST endpoints with `handlers.action(descriptor, input, securityContexts)` and register the
descriptor's path in your host router. An explicit security-context factory is required before
typed execution. Use `@Serializable` commands with `FormDecoder(Command.serializer())` and its
`springMvcInput()`, `webFluxInput()` or `ktorInput()` binding for bounded URL-encoded forms.
Do not merge query parameters into commands or bypass form limits with host parameter collectors.
Do not invent `ActionRef` or selector-based action targets.

## Safety and generated ownership

- Dynamic text goes through `text(...)`; audited sanitizer output is the only reason to opt in to
  `unsafeHtml(...)` and `raw(...)`.
- Application-local URLs use `applicationUrl(...)`; external URLs use `externalUrl(...)`. Do not bypass
  URL validation to silence the compiler.
- Treat CSS strings as CSS, not as an HTML escape hatch. Keep untrusted values out of stylesheets and
  declaration lists.
- Woge generators alone own `build/generated/ksp/main/kotlin`.
  Never edit or commit that directory; change source declarations and regenerate.
- Do not commit or serve `.woge/manifest.json`, copy it into production resources by default, or
  put secrets in its build settings. `clean` and main compilation invalidate the previous file.
- Native Declarative Partial Updates remain experimental browser syntax and are not an application
  dependency. Use the supported Woge fallback behavior.

## Enhanced pages and live regions

Use `request.context.render` for typed region targets and write `render.metadata(this)` in the HTML head.
Actions use `context.render.updates(fallback) { replace(SummaryRegion, data) }`; do not put epochs or
revisions in commands. Deferred failure HTML uses `regionHtml { ... }`. Keep protocol types in adapter
or advanced code, not page code. Configure `woge.render-identity.secret` with Base64-encoded random
bytes (at least 32) shared by all deployment instances. The unset development default is random and
process-local; Spring Boot and the Ktor config constructor warn without logging the secret.

Deferred loading HTML must include an ordinary link (optionally inside `noscript`) to a full HTML
GET, unless the document already offers the complete result. Use the typed `a` and page route APIs,
not the patch-stream URL. Shell, complete-page and patch requests share the same access checks and
read-only loader. Never put render epochs, region IDs, secrets or access tokens in the native link.
The complete GET renders final content without starting the deferred client and must be safe to reload.

For live data, declare `LiveRegionPage(page, SummaryRegion, load = { ... }, changes = { ... },
authorize = { ... })`, render `liveRegion(...)`, and bind `handlers.liveRegion(live, PageRoute)` at
that one page route. Load the shipped fallback module; no application JavaScript is needed.
`authorize` must enforce access for document, refresh and SSE reconnects; the default is anonymous.
